symptom: cks eval matrix records 'close <phase> <arm>: signal: killed' (DEV2 16, DEV4 9, FINAL2 A v2 DEV 5); every measured row is complete
mechanism: mcp-go closes stdin, waits 2 s, sends SIGTERM, waits 3 s, then SIGKILL. cks mcp catches SIGTERM and continues its deferred cleanup, so any teardown longer than about 5 s is killed.

reproduction.setup: 8 warm servers alive, 12 sequential cold ontology-arm servers

reproduction.binary: temporary phase-profiled build of the same product code

phase_profile: stdin close to stdio server return 0.00 s; the dominant teardown step is removing the materialized read tree (~1,450 files): 0.21-0.73 s; backends, jobs, footprint and leases close in <= 0.03 s
assessment: intermittent and not explained by CPU load alone; cold starts that build the same tree spiked to 18-32 s in the DEV attempt. Leading explanation: intermittent disk I/O contention on the temporary tree (confidence Mid, not proven).
product_defect_found: killed servers leave their plain source copy: 78 cks-read-source-* directories (387 MB) in the user temporary directory, oldest 2026-10-07
fix: 0fb824e5 owner-PID tagged read trees and a startup sweep of copies whose owner has exited; tests and four caught mutations; legacy unowned copies are not removed by code
not_fixed: the 5 s client grace can still be exceeded under contention; FINAL2 keeps its zero-error gate and the frozen candidate binary 7077741f does not include the sweep
